author: jakeabambo916
quote:
I’ve played every GTA since GTA3, so it hurts to write this. GTA 6 is a gorgeous game, maybe the best looking thing I’ve ever played (if you can get over 30 FPS). But somewhere in the 13 years of polishing they sanded off everything that made GTA feel like GTA. The old games felt like they were daring you to do something stupid. You’d steal a tank, cause a five-star meltdown, laugh, reload. This one feels like it wants you to behave. Everything is slow and “realistic.” Half my first night was walking, talking, watching cutscenes, and doing errands that feel more like chores than missions. There’s fishing, mini golf, working out, canoeing. Cool, I guess, but I didn’t wait over a decade for a vacation simulator. The whole game is built around the main character's relationship, and it makes everything feel careful and soft. Tommy, CJ, Niko, Trevor: none of those guys needed a hug. They were unpredictable and a little dangerous, and that was the point. Here it feels like the edge got taken away, and honestly it left me feeling kind of emasculated playing it. I’m not the guy running the city anymore, I’m the guy getting managed. 

The satire is weaker too. Earlier games roasted America with no mercy. This one pokes at Florida Man memes and social media, but it feels like it’s nervous about offending anybody. 

I’m sure a lot of critics will love this game. But for me, fun used to be the whole point of GTA, and this one seems more interested in being impressive than being fun. I put the controller down feeling bored, which I never thought I’d say about a GTA game.
